summary.text: Winnie Brinks is a Democratic member of the Michigan Senate and serves as Senate Majority Leader, the first woman to hold that position.
She is also described as the first woman to represent Grand Rapids in the Michigan Senate since Eva McCall Hamilton was elected in 1920.

paragraphs.text: Before being elected to the state House, where she served three terms, Brinks was a caseworker at The Source, director of a community-based corrections agency and a school paraprofessional.
She graduated from Calvin College with a bachelor's degree in Spanish with a concentration in sociology.
Her biography lists clean drinking water and reducing toxic PFAS chemicals, maternal health care equity, reproductive rights and prescription drug costs among her policy priorities.
She lives in Grand Rapids with her husband, Steve, a Spanish teacher; they have three daughters.
